title: Riptide source debug info (SDI)
description: Design facts imported alongside a waveform trace: a typed signal tree richer than VCD/FST, source spans for declarations and for every construct that writes or reads a signal, and the connectivity needed to compute a static cone of influence. Produced by an elaborating front end (Verilator, slang, Yosys, a simulator), never by Riptide. Read-only to the viewer: nothing here is viewer state (that is the sidecar).

version.description: SDI format major version. Riptide ignores an SDI file whose version it does not understand.

fidelity.description: What the producer actually resolved. Absent = assume the weakest level for every axis.

trace.description: How design names map onto trace paths. Absent = the defaults documented in docs/sdi.md.

files.description: Interned source files. A `span` names one by index into this array, so a path is stored once and may contain any character.

types.description: Interned type table. A `type` reference is an index into this array. Entries may reference each other by index (element/base/member types), but the graph must be acyclic apart from self-recursive class references.

units.description: Scope definitions: modules, interfaces, packages, generate blocks, named blocks, subprograms, and the synthetic scopes a dumper creates for structs and unpacked arrays. One entry per *specialization* — a parameterized module instantiated with two parameter sets is two units. Referenced by index.

warnings.description: Producer diagnostics: units it could not parse, references it could not resolve, analyses it skipped. Surfacing these is how a viewer explains an incomplete cone.

generator.description: Who produced this file and from what.

toolVersion.description: Exact version string. Required in spirit: every producer surveyed has an unversioned, drifting output format.

command.description: Command line that produced the design info, for reproduction.

sourceRoot.description: Directory that relative `files[].path` entries are relative to. Absent = the SDI file's own directory.

fidelity.description: Positive claims about what the producer actually resolved, one per axis. **Every axis is elidable, and an absent axis means "the producer said nothing", which a consumer must treat as the weakest possible claim.** So only the claim worth making is ever written, and an absent `fidelity` is the same as an empty one. This section exists because data absence alone is ambiguous: a unit with no `processes` is either a purely structural wrapper (a fact worth showing) or a unit nobody analyzed (an admission), and only the producer can tell those apart.

tree.description: complete = every scope and variable the trace can contain is present, so a signal missing from SDI is a genuine mismatch rather than an unparsed file. Absent = some scopes or variables may be missing.

types.description: declared = each variable's declared type is modelled, including enums, structs and array dimensions. Absent = types may be VCD-grade approximations, so a viewer should not offer enum decode or member slicing.

drivers.description: complete = every write and read of every variable in every unit is recorded, so an empty driver list means the signal genuinely has no driver. partial = some writers and readers are recorded but the set is not closed. Absent = no claim; treat `processes` as illustrative only.

bits.description: exact = every static part-select is recorded as a `bits` range and every non-static one carries `dynamic: true`. Absent = refs may be whole-variable regardless of what the source selected, so per-member driver queries would mislead.

coi.description: complete = the dependency graph is closed: every driver of every variable is reachable and every unanalyzable boundary is marked `blackBox`. partial = traversal may dead-end. Absent = no claim. Never claim complete when `drivers` is not complete.

traceBinding.description: How to turn a design path into the trace path a viewer resolves. Every field is a hint that removes guesswork; see "Binding to the trace" in docs/sdi.md for the resolution order.

format.description: Trace format this SDI was authored against, e.g. "vcd", "fst". Advisory.

files.description: Trace files this SDI was authored against. Advisory; never gates loading.

rootPrefix.description: Scope the dumper inserts above every design root and that has no design counterpart (Verilator's "TOP"). Prepended to every trace path.

rangeInName.description: True when the dumper appends the packed range to a vector's leaf name (VCD writes `$var reg 4 ! count [3:0]`). The loader then also tries `<name>[<msb>:<lsb>]` and `<name> [<msb>:<lsb>]`.

caseSensitive.description: False only for a dumper that folded identifier case (some VHDL flows). Riptide keys paths case-sensitively, so a producer for such a flow must emit `traceName` in the trace's own casing.

escapeStyle.description: verilog = escaped identifiers appear in the trace as `\name ` (leading backslash, trailing space). Riptide's paths have no escaping, so a producer should prefer explicit `traceName` for these.

design.description: Where elaboration starts. A trace may contain several top scopes (a testbench and a bound DUT), so roots is a list.

name.description: Trace scope name of this root, e.g. "tb". Combined with `trace.rootPrefix` to form the path prefix for everything beneath it.

decl.description: Instantiation site, when the root is instantiated from somewhere (a bind, a harness).

path.description: Path as the producer saw it. Relative paths resolve against `generator.sourceRoot`.

realPath.description: Absolute canonical path on the producing machine. Useless to a reviewer on another machine — which is why `path` + `sourceRoot` exist.

blake3.description: BLAKE3 digest (default 32-byte output, lowercase hex) of the file contents. A mismatch means the source moved under the spans, and a viewer must say so rather than render the wrong line — the failure that makes source integration worse than none. Also the only staleness check needed: it subsumes coarser guards like a line count, and unlike one it cannot itself go stale.

language.description: Source language. Drives how a viewer spells a type and how it interprets `keyword`.

span.description: Source range, positional: [file, line, col?, endLine?, endCol?]. `file` is an index into `files`. Lines and columns are 1-based; `col` 0 means unknown. `endLine` defaults to `line`; `endCol` defaults to end-of-line and is exclusive. A whole-line span is therefore [f, l] and a single token [f, l, c, l, c2].

bitRange.description: Bit slice, positional: [lsb, width]. Bit 0 is the least significant bit of the variable as the *trace* stores it — the flattened bit order the viewer already indexes samples with, not per-dimension indices. A whole-variable reference omits `bits` entirely rather than writing [0, width].

prefixItems.description: width in bits; 0 is legal and means the reference carries no bits — a void- or unit-typed signal, which still participates in dataflow

value.description: A constant, interpreted against the type it belongs to. Bit types: a string `0x…`/`0b…` (hex/binary digits, `x`/`z` allowed, `_` ignored) or a decimal integer string with optional sign; a JSON integer is also accepted when it is exact in a double. Real types: a JSON number, or "inf"/"-inf"/"nan". String types: the JSON string verbatim. Never store a wide bit value as a JSON number.

portOrdinal.description: Index into a unit's `ports` array (the port's declaration ordinal), not into `vars`.

name.description: Declared type name when the type has one (`state_e`, `hdr_t`, `std_logic_vector`). Absent for anonymous types.

spelling.description: Display form, e.g. "logic [7:0][3:0]" or "logic [7:0] $ [0:3]". A viewer shows this and switches on the structured fields.

width.description: Total flattened bit count as the trace stores the variable. REQUIRED for every bit-representable type. This is the single most valuable precomputed fact in the file: no surveyed producer emits it, every consumer needs it, and recomputing it means reimplementing the front end's width rules.

states.description: Logic value count: 2 (bit, int, VHDL bit/boolean), 4 (logic, reg, wire), 9 (VHDL std_logic). VCD bins all of these together; this is what un-bins them.

signed.description: Two's-complement interpretation. Drives the default signed/unsigned radix; VCD carries it only for `integer`, so a `logic signed [7:0]` is indistinguishable from unsigned without this.

decl.description: Where the type is declared (the typedef / enum / struct site).

comment.description: Doc comment attached to the declaration.

type.description: One entry in the interned type table, discriminated by `kind`.

typeBits.description: An elemental bit vector: `logic`, `bit`, `reg`, `wire`, `int`, `byte`, `time`, VHDL `std_logic_vector`, `unsigned`. One packed dimension is expressed here via `range`; two or more use `packedArray` over this.

keyword.description: Declared keyword, verbatim from the source language: "logic", "bit", "reg", "wire", "int", "integer", "shortint", "longint", "byte", "time", "std_logic", "std_ulogic_vector", "unsigned", "signed", "boolean", "natural". Normalized meaning lives in `width`/`states`/`signed`; this is the spelling a viewer shows and the axis VCD destroys.

range.description: Declared packed range [msb, lsb] as written, so `[0:7]` stays ascending. Display only — `bits` slices always use flattened lsb-based indices.

typeEnum.description: An enumeration. Carries the base type (so width/signedness/state count are exact) and every member with its value and declaration site — strictly more than FST's flat literal↔bitstring table.

typeStruct.description: A packed or unpacked struct or union. Member `lsb` is the flattened bit offset — required for packed aggregates because that is how a viewer slices one member out of the parent's samples, and no surveyed producer emits it.

lsb.description: Flattened bit offset within the parent. Required when `packed` is true.

value.description: Default/initial member value, when the declaration has one.

typePackedArray.description: A packed dimension over an element type: `logic [3:0][7:0]`. Element `k` occupies flattened bits [k*elemWidth, elemWidth) counting from the range's right end.

typeUnpackedArray.description: An unpacked collection. `fixed` has a declared range; the dynamic kinds have none and are typically absent from a trace entirely.

shape.description: Which unpacked collection. Only `fixed` has a `range` and a `width`; the dynamic kinds have no trace representation at all and exist here so the tree can show them as present-but-unplottable.

typeAlias.description: A typedef. Kept as its own entry so the declared name survives even when two designs share a structural type.

keyword.description: Declared spelling: "real", "shortreal", VHDL "real". Width already says 64 vs 32; this is what a viewer displays.

typeScalarOther.description: Types with no bit representation a waveform can hold: `event`, `void`, `chandle`, `virtual interface`, `class`. A variable of one of these still belongs in the tree — it shows as present but unplottable instead of vanishing, which is what VCD does to `event`.

unit.description: For `class`/`interface`: the unit that defines it.

modport.description: For an interface reference: which modport view this variable is declared against, since the direction of every signal reached through it depends on the view.

typeRefOpaque.description: An escape hatch: the producer knows a type exists but not its structure (encrypted IP, an unsupported construct). Better than lying with `bits`.

keyword.description: Whatever spelling the producer saw, even if it could not model it.

note.description: Why it is opaque — "encrypted IP", "unsupported construct". Shown to the user instead of a silently wrong type.

unit.description: A scope definition. Contents are stored once per definition, not once per instance: the elaborated tree is the walk of `design.roots` through `instances`, so file size tracks design source, not instance count.

kind.description: What kind of scope this is. `structScope`/`arrayScope` model the synthetic scopes a dumper creates when it splits a packed struct or unpacked array into one signal per member/element (Verilator's FST writer does exactly this). `blackBox` is a cell with no body.

name.description: Specialized definition name, e.g. "fifo__W8_D16". Display name for "which module is this".

origName.description: Source-level definition name before parameter specialization or mangling, e.g. "fifo".

decl.description: The definition's identifier — where "go to definition" lands. Convention for every `decl` in this format: the span covers exactly the declared name, no surrounding punctuation or type text, so a consumer can highlight the identifier without re-lexing. The one exception is an enum value, whose declaration is the whole `NAME = value`.

body.description: Full extent of the definition, first line through `endmodule`. Two things need it and neither can recover it: the source slice an RTL browser shows, and the reverse lookup from a source line to the scope that owns it (source-to-waveform cross-probing). Finding the end of a construct otherwise means a language-aware parser in the viewer — `.stems` omits it, and its consumer re-lexes the file, which fails outright for generate blocks and renders a one-line source pane.

fidelity.description: Per-unit override, for a design where only part of the source was analyzed.

params.description: Parameters and generics of this specialization, with the values it was specialized with. Two instances differing only in a parameter are two units, so these values are concrete.

local.description: localparam / constant rather than an overridable parameter.

ports.description: Port declaration order. Each entry is an index into this unit's `vars`; a port is a variable that also has a `direction`. Connections and port refs address ports by ordinal in this array, which is what makes positional connections representable.

vars.description: Every variable declared directly in this scope, in declaration order.

instances.description: Child scopes: module instantiations, generate/named blocks, subprograms, and dumper-synthesized struct/array scopes.

processes.description: Every construct that writes or reads a variable of this unit. Stored once per definition; a cone traversal instantiates it against a path. This is the section that makes both "where does this signal go" and cone of influence computable.

var.description: A declared variable, net, port, parameter or memory.

name.description: Source-level identifier, without any bit-range suffix and without hierarchy.

kind.description: How the variable is driven, independent of its value type: `net` for wire/tri/supply/VHDL signal, `var` for reg/logic/VHDL variable, `param` for a constant that never transitions, `memory` for an unpacked array a dumper may split, `alias` for a second name onto the same storage.

netType.description: Declared net/var keyword when it carries resolution semantics that `type.keyword` does not: "wire", "tri", "triand", "trior", "tri0", "tri1", "trireg", "wand", "wor", "supply0", "supply1". A viewer uses it to explain a multi-driver resolution.

direction.description: Port direction. `internal` = not a port. VCD carries none of this.

decl.description: The declaration. "Go to declaration" lands here.

value.description: Constant value for `param`, or the declared initializer.

comment.description: Doc comment on the declaration — the tooltip text.

traceName.description: Exact leaf name the dumper wrote, when it differs from `name` (a baked-in `[7:0]` suffix, an escaped identifier, a mangled name). Providing this removes all guesswork from resolution.

traceSignals.description: For one source variable that the dumper split into several trace signals — a packed struct exploded into per-member signals, an unpacked array into per-element signals, a wide net bit-blasted. Each entry maps a trace path (relative to the enclosing scope, `separator`-joined) to the slice of this variable it holds. Absent = one signal, resolved from `traceName`/`name`.

path.description: Path relative to the enclosing scope, e.g. "hdr.hi" or "mem[3]".

traceOmitted.description: Producer knows this variable is not in the trace (not dumped, optimized away, unsupported type). A viewer shows it greyed rather than reporting a failed lookup.

attrs.description: Source attributes verbatim: SystemVerilog `(* … *)`, VHDL attributes, Yosys/RTLIL attributes. Open bag, string values, never interpreted by the schema.

hints.description: Producer suggestions for presentation. A viewer may apply them as defaults; the sidecar always wins, because the sidecar is the user's decision.

role.description: Riptide maps clock/reset onto its row roles, so a design can arrive already configured.

polarity.description: With `role: "reset"` (or any active-level signal), the asserted level, so a viewer shades the band on the right value. An enum rather than a boolean because absence must mean "not stated" — a `false` would be indistinguishable from an unset default. Guessing it from waveform shape is unreliable for a design held in reset at time 0.

radix.description: Suggested default radix. An enum-typed variable implies `enum` without needing this.

group.description: Producer-defined grouping label, e.g. a bus or interface name.

hide.description: Producer considers this variable noise (a temporary, a duplicate). A viewer may collapse it by default.

instance.description: A child scope inside a unit. `unit` names the definition; everything else is per-instantiation.

name.description: Instance/scope name as it appears in the trace path, e.g. "u_fifo", "g_lane[2]".

kind.description: Matches the referenced unit's kind family. `instance` = a module/UDP instantiation with port connections; the block kinds are lexical scopes with no ports.

unit.description: The definition. Absent + `blackBox` = an opaque cell.

blackBox.description: No body available (DPI, primitive, encrypted IP). A cone traversal must then assume every input port reaches every output port; a viewer should mark the result as conservative.

decl.description: The instantiation site — where "go to instantiation" lands. FST's SOURCEISTEM carries only this, and only per scope.

array.description: Instance array range [left, right]. Trace scopes are `name[i]` for each i in the range.

inlined.description: The dumper did not create a scope for this instance; its contents appear in the parent's scope (front-end inlining, `flatten`). The path contributes nothing, and children may need `tracePrefix`.

tracePrefix.description: Prefix the dumper mangled onto every child leaf name when `inlined` is set, e.g. "u_fifo__DOT__".

params.description: Parameter overrides written at this instantiation. The resulting values live on the referenced unit's `params`; these are the source-level overrides, with locations.

conns.description: Port connections. Each carries the parent-side variables it reads and writes, so a cone traversal crosses the boundary without re-parsing an expression. An expression connection (`.a(x & y)`) simply lists several reads.

conn.description: One port connection of an instance.

port.description: Which port of the child unit. Omit only for an unresolved connection on a black box, and then give `name`.

name.description: Formal port name. Redundant with `port` but makes the file readable and survives a black box.

bits.description: Slice of the *port* this connection covers, for a partially connected port.

loc.description: The connection text in the parent — where a driver list points for a signal driven through a port.

reads.description: Parent-side variables feeding into the port (any port whose direction is input/inout, or an expression connection).

positional.description: Connected by position rather than by name.

text.description: Source text of the connection, e.g. ".dout(w_data[7:0])", so a driver list reads well without opening the file.

process.description: One RTL construct that writes and/or reads variables: a continuous assign, a procedural block, an initial block, an assertion. The unit of *sensitivity*; individual writes are its `assigns`, each with its own location.

kind.description: Which construct. `alwaysFF`/`alwaysLatch` (and any process whose sensitivity has an edge) create sequential edges; the rest are combinational. `assertion` typically has no `assigns` at all and exists purely so its reads show up in a signal's use list.

loc.description: The construct's header, e.g. the `always_ff @(...)` line.

label.description: Block name (`always_ff : main_fsm`), or the VHDL process label.

sense.description: Sensitivity list. Presence of an `edge` other than `any`/`level` is what makes this process sequential.

edge.description: Edge sensitivity. `pos`/`neg` are what classify a process as sequential, which is the single bit that separates a same-cycle cone from a whole-design one.

role.description: Semantic role. `clock`/`reset` let a viewer offer "cone within one cycle" and let Riptide auto-detect a clock without measuring waveform periods.

assigns.description: Individual writes inside the construct. One entry per lvalue statement, because the statement line is what a user wants when asking "where is this assigned".

reads.description: Reads not attributable to a single assignment: assertion expressions, `$display` arguments, loop bounds. They make a variable's use list complete without inventing a fake target.

assign.description: One write: targets on the left, everything it depends on in `sources`. Data and control dependence are distinguished by the source's `role`, not by separate lists.

loc.description: The statement. This is the location a driver list shows.

targets.description: Lvalues. Several entries for a concatenation lvalue (`{a, b} = x`).

sources.description: Everything the written value depends on, including the conditions of enclosing `if`/`case` statements (role `control`) and any non-constant index (role `index`).

delay.description: Delay/timing control as written, e.g. "#5", "@(posedge clk)". Presence means this assignment is not a same-instant function of its sources.

guarded.description: The write is conditional, so the target holds its previous value when the condition is false — a latch/enable, not a pure function of `sources`.

text.description: Single-line source text of the statement. Lets a viewer list drivers with their code even when the source files are not on the reviewer's machine.

ref.description: A reference to a bit slice of something, in the coordinate system of the enclosing unit. Exactly one of `var`, `inst`, `xmr` selects what is referenced.

oneOf.description: A variable of the enclosing unit.

loc.description: This occurrence of the identifier, when it is worth pointing at more precisely than the enclosing statement.

oneOf.description: A port of a child instance, addressed from the parent. Used when a value is taken straight off an instance port without an intermediate net.

A cross-module reference: a dotted path the producer could not or would not resolve to a local index. Resolved by the consumer against the elaborated tree; unresolvable ones widen the cone conservatively instead of breaking it.

xmr.description: Dotted path. Absolute from a design root unless it starts with ".", which means "relative to the enclosing instance path".

refUp.description: Lexical scope hops to walk up before resolving `var`/`inst`. 0 (the default) means the enclosing unit. A generate or named block referring to a signal of the module around it — the common case in real RTL — is `up: 1`. Only valid across block-like scopes (genBlock, block, function, task, structScope, arrayScope): a module, interface or program boundary is opaque, so a consumer that hits one while walking up must treat the reference as unresolved rather than crossing it.

refRole.description: Why this reference participates. `control` is a condition the write depends on, `index` a non-constant select. A cone can be filtered by role — data-only cones are far smaller and usually what a debugger wants first.

refDynamic.description: The slice was not statically known (a variable index). `bits`, if present, is a conservative bound; a consumer should widen to the whole variable and mark results approximate.

refSelect.description: Human-readable select expression as written: "hdr.hi", "mem[i]", "data[7:4]". Display only; `bits` is authoritative.
